newsitem.title: USA: Circon stake tendered by Price's Heine fund.
newsitem.headline: Circon stake tendered by Price's Heine fund.

text.p: Michael Price, who heads Heine Securities Corp, tendered his investment fund's 6.5 percent stake in Circon Corp to U.S. Surgical Corp, a spokesman for Price said on Tuesday.
"The stock was tendered," the spokesman said.
U.S. Surgical launched a hostile takeover bid for the endoscopy company Circon on August 2 at $18 a share.
On Friday Heine Securities said it held a 6.5 percent stake in Circon, or 814,700 common shares.
In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Heine said it bought the stake between August 5 and August 23 at prices ranging from $16.937 to $19.232 a share.
Circon was off 15/16 to 18-3/16 late Tuesday.

U.S. Surgical said on Friday about seven million Circon shares had been tendered. The tendered shares, added to the one million previously owned by U.S. Surgical, represent 63 percent of Circon's outstanding stock, U.S. Surgical said.
The Price spokesman was unable to say when the Heine stake had been tendered.
Circon on Friday reiterated its recommendation that shareholders not sell their shares in U.S. Surgical's $18-a-share tender, saying Circon's own strategic plan would generate "superior value."
